steps.name: Sample structure QC and low-depth sample inspection
caveats: The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its DESeq2 size factor; removal is a judgment call from the QC evidence, not a default action.
No batch/lane/run-date field exists in metadata.csv, so batch cannot be assessed or corrected for — note this limit in the QC output.
steps.context: counts.csv holds raw integer read counts for 12 samples (sample_01-06 control, sample_07-12 treated); metadata.csv holds the condition assignment. One sample is reported as shallow by the user.
steps.question: Do the 12 samples (6 control, 6 treated) separate by condition on the top-variance genes, and how does the flagged shallow sample behave relative to its group on PCA, sample-distance, and library-size metrics?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; low-depth sample keep/inspect/report per R-0008@440d

constraints: low_depth_policy = keep_inspect_report; do not delete the shallow sample silently (doi:10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8)
acceptance_criteria: Blind VST computed on the raw count matrix from counts.csv
PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, colored by condition, with sample labels
Sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap
Table of library size (total counts) and number of detected genes per sample, ranked, with the shallow sample explicitly identified and its fold-difference from the median stated
A stated, justified decision on whether the shallow sample is retained or excluded, made from the QC evidence, not by default

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: If the count source turns out to be length-scaled (e.g., matches TPM/FPKM behavior against the gene-length file), the count model's assumptions are violated; report this rather than silently modeling anyway.
GC-content/gene-length bias correction tools (cqn, EDASeq) are absent from this environment; run the log-ratio-vs-length/GC diagnostic if feasible and state the finding, but do not block on it.
With n=6 per group, DESeq2 flags (not replaces) count outliers via Cook's distance and sets padj to NA for flagged genes — report these separately from independent-filtering NAs.
steps.context: Two-group, unpaired, n=6 vs 6 design, no batch field, raw counts. gene_length_reference.csv exists but its role (length-scaling correction) is not yet confirmed against counts.csv.
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated (sample_07-12) and control (sample_01-06), controlling FDR at 0.05?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, two-group n=6/6 design, per R-0029@22ca / R-0001@9a17

constraints: size_factors = median_of_ratios (DESeq2 internal), no pre-normalization of counts before the model (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8)
reference_level explicit = control; contrast named condition, treated, control (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#note-on-factor-levels)
independent_filtering = true, alpha = 0.05, adjustment = BH, filter results by adjusted p-value only (doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107; doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x)
acceptance_criteria: Count provenance stated: counts.csv inspected for integrality and value range against the separate gene-length file before modeling; if a length-correction ambiguity remains, it is reported explicitly rather than assumed away
Minimal pre-filter applied: gene kept if >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size)
DESeq2 design ~condition with condition releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference
Wald test contrast named as condition, treated, control (positive log2FC = higher in treated)
apeglm shrinkage applied to the treated-vs-control coefficient; results table carries both unshrunken and shrunken log2FoldChange plus lfcSE
Independent filtering left on; results() called with alpha=0.05; BH-adjusted p-values used for gene selection, never raw p-values
P-value histogram plotted and inspected before trusting the adjustment
MA plot and dispersion plot produced as fit diagnostics
Genes with NA padj from independent filtering vs from Cook's-distance outlier flagging are reported separately with counts
Decision on the shallow sample from T1S1 applied consistently in the DESeq2 sample sheet

steps.name: fgsea preranked Hallmark pathway enrichment
caveats: Do not run over-representation analysis on a short significant-gene list; the ranked preranked method on the full tested list is the method of record here.
Enrichment results are method-dependent; present pathways as hypotheses for follow-up, not proven findings, and report the Hallmark vs Reactome overlap/disagreement.
steps.context: Human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) are available at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/, and Reactome pathway gene sets (all species, HGNC symbols) at /mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways/current/ — filter the Reactome GMT to human pathways using the accompanying species index file before testing.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes changing between treated and control, using the full ranked gene list from the DESeq2 Wald statistic?

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark per R-0098@d01b, disputed rank-metric side resolved to Wald stat per R-0108@409f

constraints: rank_metric = stat (Wald statistic), disputed choice R-0108@409f resolved to the Wald statistic side (doi:10.1101/060012; doi:10.1186/s12859-017-1674-0)
gene_set_collection = msigdb_hallmark_human, then reactome_pathways as the second collection, each with its release stated (doi:10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004; doi:10.1093/nar/gkz1031)
id_mapping = to gene symbols matching the GMT identifier space, with org.Hs.eg.db as needed; report unmapped share (doi:10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100141)
acceptance_criteria: All tested genes (post pre-filter) ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column), no pre-thresholding on padj or fold change
Gene symbols mapped to the identifier space of the gene set collection; unmapped share reported
fgsea run against MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets), size window 15-500 genes among tested genes
BH-adjusted p-values reported per pathway; leading-edge genes listed for every pathway at padj < 0.05
Second pass against Reactome pathway gene sets from the reference store, same rank metric and size window, with the Reactome release stated
Redundant/overlapping significant gene sets collapsed and reported as one finding with a representative name and full member table kept as supplement
Hallmark and Reactome results kept as separate tables, never merged into one ranked list

steps.name: Consolidated DE and pathway enrichment report
caveats: No subject/donor identifier separate from 'sample' exists in metadata.csv, so biological independence of replicates cannot be confirmed — state this as a design limitation.
No batch/lane/run-date field is present, so batch effects cannot be assessed or corrected for — state this as a design limitation.
steps.context: Consolidates outputs of T1S1 (QC), T1S2 (DE), and T2S1 (enrichment) into one report for the research question of which genes and which Hallmark pathways change between treated and control.
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible summary of the treated-vs-control gene expression changes and Hallmark/Reactome pathway changes, including the low-depth sample decision?

grounding.reason: no rule covers the report step directly; assembled from the report-related claims returned for the DE and enrichment steps

constraints: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
acceptance_criteria: Gene table with unshrunken log2FC, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, padj for every tested gene, ranked by shrunken log2FC for display
MA plot and dispersion plot included as fit diagnostics
P-value histogram included with a stated interpretation of its shape
Method section states: DESeq2 version, apeglm version, fgsea version, design formula, named contrast, alpha, count source determination, and the low-depth sample decision with its rationale
Number of genes tested after filtering and number significant at padj<0.05 reported

title: Treated vs control DE + Hallmark pathway enrichment
analytical_narrative: Twelve human bulk RNA-seq samples (6 control: sample_01-06, 6 treated: sample_07-12), raw integer counts in counts.csv, condition assignment in metadata.csv, gene lengths in a separate reference file. One sample is flagged as shallow by the user. The plan first runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size table) so the low-depth sample is inspected and its removal, if any, is a stated decision rather than a silent default — per the retrieved evidence, DESeq2's per-sample size factor already accounts for depth, so a low-depth sample is down-weighted, not excluded, unless QC shows it is an outlier or a failed library. Counts then go through a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 6 samples, the smallest group size), DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit control-vs-treated contrast, apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 — the grounded two-group DESeq2 template. Because the profile does not state whether the counts are gene-length-corrected (import_state unknown), the DE step first inspects the count table (value range, integrality) and the standalone gene-length file, and records what it establishes about count provenance before modeling, rather than assuming length-scaled counts. The ranked DESeq2 Wald statistic feeds fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (50 sets, min/max size 15-500), followed by Reactome pathways as the second collection per the grounded rule, both from the reference store. A final report step consolidates the DE table (unshrunken and shrunken log2FC), the two enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the p-value histogram, and a full reproducibility record.
